subject: On-prem inference network decision log & measurement plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa@finsolve.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@finsolve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick network checks and measurement plan

Hi Lisa / Carlos —

Thanks for the call this morning. Recap and proposed next steps focused on the on-prem/VPC performance questions we discussed. I want to keep this tight so the engineering teams can run the tests we need to validate production readiness.

High-level goals (what we need to validate):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end inference (client -> customer gateway -> Redwood runtime -> response) target <= 120 ms for single-request streaming workloads.
- Concurrency: sustain 200 concurrent streaming sessions with median CPU/GPU utilization within expected band (pilot numbers will be validated).
- Burst behavior: handle 4k-token bursts from the client with streaming gRPC without head-of-line blocking.
- Throughput: 600 tokens/sec aggregate across the pool during steady-state for the pilot load.

Immediate asks for your infra team (Carlos):
1) Run and share a 3-minute traceroute/mtr from your inference clients to the documented VPN endpoint. Export as PNG and attach.
2) Share the VPN BGP peer IPs and whether NAT is applied on the customer edge (we need to know source IP preservation for session affinity).
3) Provide a sample payload pattern (typical request size and average token count) plus expected concurrency distribution (p90/p99).

Ben / Vivek — can you review the test checklist below and confirm if we should add any Redwood-specific probes (tcpdump capture points, custom header checks)?

Suggested measurement plan (we can run these from your side or via a short window where Redwood agents run in your VPC):
- Step A: baseline iperf3 (TCP) to the Redwood VPN endpoint for 3 x 60s runs.
- Step B: MTR with 200 packets to profile per-hop jitter/loss.
- Step C: gRPC streaming smoke test (10 streams, 30s) with short and long payloads to observe prefix caching behavior.
- Step D: synthetic load run that simulates your 95th percentile request size for 5 minutes while we capture p50/p95/p99 latency.

Attachments referenced: traceroute stub, vpn config example, iperf sample template.

Proposed owners & timeline:
- Carlos to run Steps A-B and attach results by EOD Thu (03/11).
- Redwood (Ben) to provide iperf/GRPC client scripts and an instrumentation checklist by EOD Wed (03/10).
- Decision checkpoint: Fri (03/12) 10:30am PT — we agree go/no-go for pilot.

If any of the targets above look off relative to your expectations, flag them and we can re-align.

Thanks —
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
(attachment: iperf3-sample-output.csv, type: text/csv)
From: Lisa Chang <lisa@finsolve.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@finsolve.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick network checks and measurement plan

Thanks Rishi — good summary. Carlos and I split the asks across teams; a couple of clarifications below and a quick note on timing.

Clarifications:
- NAT: our edge appliance does 1:1 NAT for outbound sessions from the inference cluster, but sessions originating from application clients preserve the source IP when routed through the internal firewall in our VPC.
- VPN: we are using a managed VPN (vendor: CloudEdge) with BGP. I attached the VPN endpoint config and the public peer IPs.
- Payloads: typical request sizes are small (avg ~220 tokens), but we have a long-tail of 3–4k token generation requests ~2% of traffic.

Carlos will run the traceroute/mtr and attach the screenshot. We expect to have Step A-B artifacts to you by end of day Thursday (03/11).

Attachments: traceroute-finsolve-0309.png (PNG) and vpn-endpoint-config.txt (text).

Best,
Lisa Chang
Head of Infrastructure, FinSolve
(attachment: traceroute-finsolve-0309.png, type: image/png)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@finsolve.com>, Lisa Chang <lisa@finsolve.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick network checks and measurement plan

Thanks; saw the VPN config and traceroute image — useful. Quick interpretation and added test guidance from Redwood SRE side.

Interpretation of traceroute: there are two asymmetric hops in the middle of the path that explain the 30–40ms variance in a few probes; not fatal but worth monitoring for packet reorder during bursts.

Extra tests I recommend we run (scripts attached in the shared Drive link):
- iperf3: 3 x 60s TCP and UDP runs, with -P 10 parallel streams to show aggregate behavior. Capture CPU on both ends.
- mtr: 10-minute run saved as CSV to identify intermittent loss windows.
- tcpdump: 60s capture during a 1-minute synthetic 4k-token burst to look for retransmits and retrans timing.

Network tuning suggestions to reduce variability during bursts:
- Set MTU to 1500 across the VPN tunnel; if CloudEdge supports jumbo frames we can test 9000 but keep parity.
- Increase TCP window scaling for the application subnet (suggested tcp_rmem/tcp_wmem adjustments).
- Enable BGP MD5 where possible for peer stability.

Success criteria (pass/fail for pilot):
- No more than 0.5% packet loss on sustained 5-minute runs.
- p95 end-to-end streaming latency <= 120 ms for 95% of 5-minute windows during synthetic load.
- No session resets or gRPC stream errors during a 4k-token burst test.

I'll drop the iperf and gRPC client scripts in the Drive folder and link them in the HubSpot deal. Ben (SE) will run the gRPC smoke test remotely if you can open a port to the Redwood test agent, otherwise we can run from your side.

Action items I can take:
- Upload scripts by EOD Wed (03/10).
- Run a verified smoke test remotely Thu morning if port is open.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: vpn-endpoint-config.txt, type: text/plain)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chang <lisa@finsolve.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@finsolve.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Decision log & owners — FinSolve on-prem pilot readiness

Quick decision log following artifacts and internal review. Thanks to everyone for the fast turnaround.

What we received:
- Traceroute and VPN config from FinSolve (Carlos) — shows asymmetric hops but no sustained loss.
- Confirmation on NAT behavior and payload distribution (Lisa).

Redwood assessment (Vivek / Ben):
- Conditions look acceptable for a small pilot with the following mitigations in place: TCP window tuning, 1500 MTU baseline, and active monitoring for packet reorder.
- We will use a model variant with smaller KV cache footprints for the pilot to reduce memory pressure during concurrency bursts and fall back to a larger variant if quality/regression tests pass.

Owners and next steps:
- Carlos: run Steps A-B (iperf3, mtr) and upload CSVs by EOD Thu (03/11) — RECEIVED.
- Ben: upload iperf and gRPC client scripts to Drive and run the smoke test Thurs morning (03/11).
- Vivek: confirm fallback model variant and rollout policy by Thu EOD.
- Laura: start procurement request for any required network appliances if iperf indicates sustained throughput shortfall (>20% below target) — initial budget estimate needed by Mon (03/15).

Decision: Proceed to pilot window (2-day pilot) starting Tue (03/16) assuming no showstopper in the iperf/gRPC runs. Final go/no-go to be confirmed at checkpoint call Mon (03/15) 10am PT.

Links: HubSpot deal and shared Drive in the thread metadata.

Thanks — keep updates in the thread so we have a single source of truth.

Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
